Attach spatial covariates

Source: R/covariates.R
bruce_covariates.Rd

Extracts covariates at station locations and at background cells, standardises them, and keeps the rasters for prediction.

Usage

bruce_covariates(
  d,
  rasters,
  background_method = "buffer_mean",
  background_buffer = 5500,
  scale_on = NULL
)

Arguments

d

A bruce_data object.

rasters

A terra::SpatRaster whose layer names are the covariate names (syntactic R names), e.g. elev, urb, svf.

background_method

How each covariate is represented at background cells: "buffer_mean" (mean within background_buffer metres, matching the footprint of a coarse grid cell), "point" (value at the cell centre), or "zero" (set to the covariate mean; for covariates that have no meaning at the background's scale, such as sky view factor). A single value or a named vector per covariate.

background_buffer

Buffer radius in metres for "buffer_mean".

scale_on

Which locations define the standardisation of each covariate: "background" or "stations". Defaults to "background" when a background exists and the covariate is not "zero", otherwise "stations".

Value

d with a covariates element.

Details

Covariate values that are missing after extraction are set to the covariate mean (0 on the standardised scale). The observed range at stations and background cells is stored and used by bruce_predict() to cap covariates on the prediction grid, so the model never extrapolates a linear effect beyond the data.
